Section 1 – General Information

1.1 Purpose. The District Board of Trustees of Lakeridge State College (the “College”) is soliciting proposals from qualified firms to provide complete custodial services, including all labor, supervision, equipment, cleaning chemicals, sanitizers, soap and paper consumables, for the College campuses and centers identified in Section 2. One (1) contract will be awarded to the responsive and responsible proposer whose proposal is determined to be most advantageous to the College.

1.2 Term of Contract. The contract resulting from this RFP shall be for an initial term of three (3) years beginning July 1, 2027, with the option to renew for two (2) additional one (1) year periods upon mutual written agreement, for a maximum term of five (5) years.

1.3 Current Contract. Custodial services are presently provided under Contract No. LSC-21-117, awarded in April 2021 to Meridian Building Care, Inc., which expires June 30, 2027. Expenditures under the current contract for fiscal year 2025-2026 were $2,186,400. This information is provided for reference only and does not represent a guaranteed level of compensation under the new contract.

1.4 Pre-Proposal Meeting. Attendance at the pre-proposal meeting and site visit is mandatory. The site visit will begin at the Winter Haven Campus and proceed to the Lakeland Campus; proposers are responsible for visiting the centers listed in Section 2.3.4 on their own.

Section 2 – Scope of Work

2.1 General. The Contractor shall provide custodial services at all buildings listed in Table 2-1 at the frequency and cleaning level shown. Cleaning standards are defined by the APPA Custodial Staffing Guidelines for Educational Facilities. Unless otherwise noted, all interior areas of each building are included: classrooms, laboratories, offices, corridors, stairwells, elevators, restrooms, locker rooms, break rooms, lobbies and entrances.

2.2 Billing. The College will pay a monthly fee computed as the proposed price per square foot multiplied by the estimated gross square footage of each building listed for billing purposes. When a room or building is taken out of service during construction or remodeling, the Contractor will be relieved of all or part of the contract obligations for the area designated and the monthly payment will be reduced by the square footage taken out of service.

2.3 Locations and List of Buildings to be used for Billing Purposes

Table 2-1 lists the buildings included in this solicitation. Floor plans and a list of rooms and square footage of each room is available for review at the Purchasing Department.

2.3.1 Days of Service. “M–F” means Monday through Friday; “M–Sa” means Monday through Saturday; “7 days” means every day of the year except College holidays listed in Exhibit E; “M/W/F” means Monday, Wednesday and Friday; “T/Th” means Tuesday and Thursday; “1x/wk” means once per week on a day designated by the Facilities Director.

2.3.2 Facilities Not Included. The following facilities are not part of this solicitation: Building WPE (Physical Education Annex), which was demolished in June 2025; the Lakeland Collegiate High School building (LCH), which is cleaned by the County School Board under a separate agreement; and the Winter Haven Campus Central Energy Plant (WEP), which is maintained by College staff.

2.3.3 Modular Buildings. Modular buildings are billed as a group at the combined square footage shown. The seven (7) Winter Haven modular buildings range from 960 to 1,124 square feet each; the four (4) Lakeland modular buildings (LMA, LMB, LMC and LMD) are 1,938 square feet each.

2.3.4 Center Addresses. JD Alexander Center, 210 East Park Avenue, Lake Wales; Lake Wales Arts Center, 1150 Scenic Highway South, Lake Wales; Airside Center, 3260 Flightline Drive, Lakeland; Bartow Center, 2250 Clear Springs Road, Bartow; Clear Springs Advanced Technology Center, 2260 Clear Springs Road, Bartow; Haines City Center, 31 East Hinson Avenue, Suite 4, Haines City.

2.4 Hours of Service

2.4.1 Routine cleaning at locations designated “M–F” shall be performed between 5:00 p.m. and 1:30 a.m., Monday through Friday, so that buildings are ready for occupancy by 7:00 a.m. Locations designated “M–Sa” receive an additional Saturday shift between 7:00 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. Locations designated “7 days” shall be cleaned nightly and receive weekend day service between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m.

2.4.2 The Contractor shall provide one (1) day porter at the Winter Haven Campus and one (1) day porter at the Lakeland Campus, Monday through Friday from 7:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., to restock restrooms, respond to spills and service high-traffic areas. Day porter hours are included in the price per square foot.

2.4.3 The Contractor shall provide event services (set-up, monitoring and clean-up) on request at the hourly rate proposed on the Price Proposal Form. Approximately 400 event hours per year are anticipated; event hours are not billed by square foot.

2.4.4 The Contractor shall staff a minimum of one (1) on-site supervisor per campus during each evening shift and shall provide a project manager available Monday through Friday during business hours.

2.5 Cleaning Requirements

  1. Restrooms: clean and disinfect all fixtures, partitions and floors at each scheduled service; restock soap, paper towels, toilet tissue and seat covers.
  2. Floors: dust mop and damp mop hard floors; vacuum carpet at each service; spot clean carpet as needed. Periodic scrub-and-recoat of resilient tile is required twice per year (winter and summer breaks); strip-and-refinish once per year.
  3. Trash and recycling: empty all receptacles and transport to the designated dumpster or compactor.
  4. Classrooms and laboratories: clean tables, desks, chalk and marker boards; laboratory benches are cleaned by College staff only.
